back: A method of moving goods or people: road, rail, air, water or pipeline.
The gap in **place** between producers and consumers (place utility).
Door-to-door delivery and flexibility of route and time; best over short distances.
Heavy, bulky goods over long distances: coal, minerals, cement, fertiliser, grain, containers.
Perishable, urgent or valuable goods: cut flowers, fresh produce for export, medicines, documents, spare parts.
Liquids and gases: fuel, water, natural gas, sewage.
Liners sail fixed routes to timetables; tramps have no fixed route and are hired for particular cargoes.
It is the slowest mode and reaches only ports, so a landlocked country also needs road or rail.

front: Give three reasons transport is important to commerce.
back: Bridges the gap in place; widens markets and allows specialisation; stabilises prices by moving goods to shortage areas; creates jobs (any three).
